resolution_boundary.next_step: A later resolution proposal must identify declaration IDs and bind new evidence; this view is not a completed resolution ledger.
resolution_boundary.statement: Measurements are observations, not automatic resolutions of natural-language declarations. Geometry pass does not prove physical performance, manufacturing, missing inputs or every clause of a compound declaration.

open_blockers.claim: The as-printed CAD pose is presented as the rest pose, and all rest checks are measured there: rest-button-shell, outer-form-matches-base, no_operation_at_rest, and the flush face in assembly.png. That pose is not in equilibrium once a switch is fitted. The leaf is stress-free in that pose and nothing holds the button from moving outward. The switch pin is drawn touching the dog point, 0.2 mm into its 0.35 mm pretravel, so the pin pushes the button out. Using the recipe's own stiffness (k_tip 2.125 N/mm x (8.5/19.5)^2 = 0.40 N/mm at the plunger), any pin force F moves the plunger out by F/0.40 mm. Release-force minima from the registered datasheets give 0.05-0.34 N, i.e. 0.12-0.85 mm or 0.36-2.5 deg outward. The rise check covers only +0.3 deg. The stated adjustment procedure also fails: turning the screw in until the switch operates needs the leaf to carry the operating force (up to 1.47 N). That means about 3.6 mm (about 10.7 deg) of outward plunger motion, and root stress of about 40 MPa against the 23.5 MPa allowance. My rigid probe shows the button reaches the shell at about 5 deg outward (0.013 mm left), so the window edge would act as an unplanned, unchecked stop. The flush outer form and the click-referenced rest offset therefore hold only with no switch fitted.
evidence: recipe: no outward stop. design_basis says "No pin, spring, rest or stop screws"; rotation_checks rise-clear-of-shell end_deg 0.3.

switch_pin STEP top y=22.8 = actuator tip (overlap-actuator_screw-switch_pin distance 3.6e-15); switch_body top y=22.302, so the pin protrudes 0.4975 mm against zippy FP 7.35 - body 6.65 = 0.70 mm, i.e. 0.20 mm pre-pressed.
switch_profiles.py release_force: zippy S 35 gf min, L 21 gf; omron 20 gf (low-force 5 gf); operating_force up to 150 gf (1.47 N).

measurements leaf-spring-beam: stiffness 2.125 N/mm at a tip deflection of 0.6229 mm gives 1.324 N and 15.88 MPa. Scaling to the 3.37 N tip force needed for 1.47 N at the plunger gives about 40 MPa, against 23.5 MPa allowed.

Own probe (CadQuery 2.8, button+screw rotated about (-17.5,26.5) on z): outward +0.3 deg 0.375 mm, +1.0 deg 0.318 mm, +2.5 deg 0.200 mm, +5.0 deg 0.013 mm to shell. Button bbox ymax rises 0.11 / 0.33 / 0.87 mm at +0.36 / +1.0 / +2.5 deg.
FLOW_RESULT 8_recipe switch_profile_fit no_operation_at_rest 0.025 mm is a rigid-pose margin with no leaf compliance.
open_blockers.proposed_change: Make the rest pose an equilibrium, or stop claiming it is one. Options: (a) add an outward hard stop, such as a shell lip or tab catching the button, and preload the leaf against it so the stop reaction exceeds the largest pin force at rest; or (b) print the leaf pre-deflected so the as-printed pose is the preloaded rest; or (c) stiffen the leaf until the preload deflection fits inside a stated rise envelope. Then rewrite the adjustment step so it does not require the leaf to carry the operating force.
open_blockers.required_test: Add a check that computes the rest pose from leaf stiffness and the largest registered pin force at rest, with the stop modelled. Extend rise-clear-of-shell to that angle plus margin. Run outer-form-matches-base (or a protrusion check) on the button at that pose. Add a flexure load case for the adjustment procedure (operating force through the leaf) against the stress allowance. Add a blocked rotation check showing the button hits the intended outward stop before the window edge, at every axis offset.

open_blockers.claim: The stated rest pose cannot exist once the switch is set by the stated procedure. The procedure (turn in until the switch operates, out until it releases, then 3 x 1/16 turn out) leaves the dog point 0.075-0.195 mm above the release point, which is still inside the switch pretravel. So the pin pushes outward on the button with at least the release force. In revision 14 the only thing reacting that force is the leaf. There is no rest screw or rest stop. The leaf is soft at the plunger: 0.40 N/mm by the recipe's own PRBM numbers and about 0.27 N/mm by linear beam theory with the load at the plunger. So the button rises out of the skin by about RF/k. Zippy S (RF >= 35 gf = 0.34 N): 0.85-1.28 mm at the plunger, 2.5-3.8 deg, about 1.4-2.1 mm proud at the far edge. Zippy L (21 gf): 0.51-0.77 mm, 1.5-2.3 deg. OMRON low force (5 gf): 0.36-0.54 deg. Every one of these is larger than the 0.3 deg that rise-clear-of-shell covers. The operate step itself needs about OF/k = 1.47/0.40 = 3.6 mm (about 10.8 deg) of outward travel. My probe shows the button touches the shell window edge at about 5 deg outward. So during adjustment the shell, not the leaf, reacts the switch, and the setting is made against an unintended contact. As a result the outer-form check, the rest clearance, no_operation_at_rest and the click angles were all evaluated at a pose (leaf unstressed, pin force zero) that the documented process does not produce. The click stroke from the real rest also includes this extra ~0.5-1.3 mm of soft travel.
evidence: side_button_leaf_recipe.py: rest_window_mm = (3*0.025, MD + 4*0.025) above OP; switch_body placed so OP is 0.148 mm below the tip; switch_pin modeled only up to the tip (0.4975 mm) while zippy FP max - body = 7.35 - 6.65 = 0.70 mm.
switch_profiles.py: zippy release_force 35 gf min (L 21 gf), operating_force 150 gf max; omron release_force 20 gf min (low-force 5 gf).
measurements.json leaf-spring-beam: stiffness 2.125 N/mm at leaf tip; beam_force_ratio 0.4359 (8.5/19.5) -> plunger stiffness 2.125*0.4359^2 = 0.404 N/mm.
Own calculation (linear Euler-Bernoulli, E = 1.7 GPa as in _flexure_check, load 11 mm beyond the leaf tip at x=2): plunger compliance (L^3/3 + aL^2 + a^2 L)/EI = 3.73 mm/N -> 0.268 N/mm.
recipe rotation_checks: rise-clear-of-shell end_deg +0.3 (0.10 mm at the 19.5 mm plunger lever).

Own CadQuery probe on exported STEP (button + actuator_screw rotated about (-17.5, 26.5) +z vs shell): +1 deg 0.318 mm, +2 deg 0.239 mm, +3 deg 0.161 mm, +5 deg 0.013 mm, +8 deg overlap 0.19 mm3; contact near (-10.4, 31.25, 10.0), the near window edge.

design_basis assumption: "Adjustment (switch fitted, output read): with the button at rest turn the actuator screw in until the switch operates, out until it releases, then 3 steps of 1/16 turn further out."
switch_fit_leaf no_operation_at_rest is a rigid-stack margin (0.025 mm) that assumes the button stays at the rest pose under pin force.
open_blockers.proposed_change: Make the rest reference consistent with a leaf-only button. One option is a zero-preload rest: put the dog point above the switch free position. The setting procedure then holds the button flush with a gauge or fixture, turns in until the switch operates, and backs out by PT max plus a stated gap (zippy 0.62 + gap). Re-derive click_nominal and click_latest and the force basis from that stroke. The other option is an explicit outward rest stop on the shell (ledge against the pad or spine) with the leaf preloaded inward by more than the largest pin force at rest. Model that stop and keep the procedure. Either way, model the rest pin force explicitly and state the resulting protrusion. Do not leave the pin drawn as truncated at the tip.
open_blockers.required_test: Add a rest-equilibrium check for every switch profile: u_rest = F_pin(rest) / k_plunger, with F_pin from RF min to OF max and k from both the PRBM and the beam-with-moment models. Require u_rest <= a stated tolerance, or a rest stop that a blocked rotation check proves engaged. Run outer-form, rest clearance and rise checks at the worst u_rest pose, not at +0.3 deg. Also simulate the operate step (u = OF/k) and show it does not drive the button into the shell. Physical test after printing: measure button protrusion and click travel after the documented procedure with each fitted switch.

open_blockers.claim: The stated rest pose, and every check made there, assume a rigid rest, but the button hangs only on a compliant leaf and the switch pin pushes it outward. With the recipe's own numbers (leaf 2.125 N/mm at the tip, moment ratio 8.5/19.5), the stiffness at the plunger is about 0.40 N/mm. The stated adjustment procedure sets rest by force balance near the release point, where the pin force is about RF. RF is at least 0.34 N (zippy S, 35 gf min), so the button would rest roughly 0.85 mm outward at the plunger, about 2.5 deg, with the far edge of the face about 1.3 mm proud of the skin. The rise check covers only +0.3 deg. The step "turn in until the switch operates" needs up to OF 1.47 N (150 gf max), which means about 3.6 mm (about 10.6 deg) outward. Applying the recipe's own beam formula there gives about 40 MPa in the leaf, against the 23.5 MPa allowance. So rest-button-shell, rise-clear-of-shell, outer-form-matches-base and the switch-fit check no_operation_at_rest (0.025 mm) are all evaluated at a pose the stated procedure does not produce. The design states this pose as the rest, so the outer-form preference ("外形はできるだけ変えないで") is reported as kept at rest without evidence.
evidence: recipe design_basis: "Adjustment ... with the button at rest turn the actuator screw in until the switch operates, out until it releases, then 3 steps of 1/16 turn further out."
measurements leaf-spring-beam: stiffness_n_per_mm 2.125, beam_force_ratio 0.4359 (8.50 mm / 19.50 mm). Plunger stiffness = 2.125 x (8.5/19.5)^2 is about 0.40 N/mm.
switch_profiles.py zippy_df_pin: release_force 35 gf min (S), operating_force 150 gf max (S); FP 7.35 max, OP 7.0 +/-0.2 above body bottom.
STEP probe: switch_pin y 22.3025..22.8 and actuator tip y 22.8. The tip is at OP+0.1475 mm, below FP (OP+0.35 max), so the pin is drawn pressed by up to 0.2 mm at rest.

STEP probe: the button rotated outward about (-17.5, 26.5) stays clear of the shell at 0.3/1/2/3/5 deg (0.375/0.318/0.239/0.161/0.013 mm), so nothing limits the outward float. rise-clear-of-shell checks only to +0.3 deg.

Stress at the adjustment pose: tip deflection sin(10.6 deg) x 8.5 is about 1.56 mm, F = 2.125 x 1.56 is about 3.3 N, sigma = F x 10 x 0.5 / 0.4167 is about 40 MPa, above allowed_mpa 23.5 (formula from recipe.py _flexure_check).

switch_fit_leaf no_operation_at_rest: value_mm 0.025 = 0.075 - 0.05. This is a rigid-stack screw offset; with leaf compliance most of the 0.075 mm back-off goes into leaf relaxation, not pin clearance.
open_blockers.proposed_change: Make the rest pose consistent with the force path. One option is a geometric outward rest stop on the shell, preloading the leaf inward so the leaf preload exceeds the largest registered pin force at rest. Another is a leaf/lever ratio stiff enough that the pin force moves the rest by a stated small amount. Then rewrite the adjustment procedure so it works with the compliant support, and recompute no_operation_at_rest with the compliance included. Until then, label the modelled rest pose and the outer-form-at-rest claim UNVERIFIED in unverified_requirements.
open_blockers.required_test: For each complete switch profile, compute the rest equilibrium angle from the leaf stiffness and the pin force range (RF min to OF max, plus the pin pre-compression at the modelled tip position). Rerun rise-clear-of-shell and the outer-form/bulge comparison of the button at that angle. Check leaf stress at the adjustment pose (switch operating with no thumb force) against the 0.5 x yield allowance. Recompute the rest margin to the release point with the compliance included and pivot play subtracted.

open_blockers.claim: The stated manufacturing route (one FDM print, shell rim-down, leaf and button printed in place, '0.4 mm running gap separates face and shell on all sides') does not produce a free button in that orientation, and nothing checks or labels this. Rim-down, the window's top and bottom running gaps are horizontal: the shell lintel's downward face at z=18.4 is a ~25 mm unsupported bridge (x -10.4..14.6) hanging 0.4 mm over the button top at z=18, and the button's lower skin strips at z=10 are printed 0.4 mm above the shell sill. In addition the button is an unanchored island for its first 1 mm: its lowest faces are at z=10 (skin strips and plunger), but the leaf and pad that join it to anything only start at z=11. So the first button layers need support; under the plunger that support can stand on the bed, but under the skin strips it would have to sit in the 0.4 mm slot on the sill, where it cannot be removed. Without it the strips droop onto the sill. Either way the face is likely to fuse to the shell at its top and bottom edges, which defeats the 'printed in place, free running gap' claim. The unverified list only says 'print-in-place gap ... depend[s] on printer calibration', which does not disclose an orientation and overhang conflict that is purely geometric.
evidence: My CadQuery probe on the exported STEPs: button downward-facing planar faces at z=10.00 (areas 13.13, 13.05, 6.90 mm2 on the skin strips, y 29.5-31.8; 31.97 mm2 on the plunger), at z=11.00 (pad, 9.91 mm2) and at z=12.60 (spine). Leaf bottom at z=11.00 (10 mm2). Button bbox z 10.0-18.0, leaf bbox z 11.0-16.0.

Vertical ray probe: from the button bottom strips at z=10 (x=-9..13.5, y=30.0-31.5) the shell is reached 0.42 mm below (sampling step 0.02 mm), i.e. the 0.4 mm gap sits directly above the sill. From the button top at z=18 (x=-9..13.5) the shell lintel is 0.42 mm above. Shell downward face at z=18.40 spans x -10.4..14.61, y 27.26..29.86 (37.81 mm2).
Below the plunger bottom (x=2, y=25, z=10) there is no shell within 12 mm, so it needs a 10 mm support column from the bed.

Recipe design_basis: 'Printed in place with the shell (rim-down); the 0.4 mm running gap separates face and shell on all sides.' The outputs give manufacturing_process 'FDM ... printed in place' for shell, leaf_spring and button.
measurements.json check kinds: no overhang, support, bridging or island check; verification_plan has no printability item.
open_blockers.proposed_change: Make the stated route printable, or change the stated route. Option A: change the window's top and bottom gap faces (on both the shell and the button) to self-supporting slopes. For a rim-down print, cut them at an angle so that no horizontal face of the button or shell lies directly over the other part across the gap. Also give the button's lowest layer an anchor: start the leaf/pad at or below the button's lowest z, or add a declared break-off sprue to the shell. Option B: declare a different orientation or process (for example, print the button and leaf separately and attach them), with the part count and assembly step stated. In both cases add a declared support/overhang statement to the contract (which faces need support, where support goes, how it is removed) and mark print-in-place success as UNKNOWN until printed.
open_blockers.required_test: Run an automated downward-facing-face scan in the declared build direction, for each printed part. Report each face with a normal below a stated overhang limit together with what lies under it: the bed, another printed part (and the gap), or nothing. Fail when a face sits over another part across a gap smaller than the declared support-plus-clearance, and fail when a part's lowest layer has no connection to the bed or to support. Then do a physical print of the stated orientation: confirm that the button deflects freely with no fused edges, and record the slicer settings.
